title: What if the one you stop is rightly guided?
subtitle: A gentle question before the warning

row.title: I am sure he is wrong

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}first admonished him with what was better{/idea}: do you think this man you are stopping is upon the straight path in his action? {reward}Before any threat, a question.{/reward}
now: Your teenager starts wearing hijab, or your friend starts going to the mosque, and your first reaction is to argue them out of it. {idea}Pause and ask: what if they are on the right path?{/idea}
old: I know better than them what is good for them.
new: Before I oppose someone's good, I should ask if they are the one who is guided.
try: Think of someone whose choice you have criticized. Ask yourself honestly if they might be right.

title: Or if he is calling people to be mindful of Allah?
subtitle: His words, not just his actions
then: Ibn Kathir: is he upon guidance in his action, {idea}or enjoining taqwa in his statements{/idea}? {trap}Yet you rebuke him and threaten him for his prayer.{/trap}
now: Someone in the family chat shares a reminder about prayer and gets mocked. {idea}Their message was a call to be mindful.{/idea} You do not have to agree with the delivery to respect the call.
old: People who give reminders are just being preachy.
new: Someone urging taqwa deserves a hearing, not a rebuke.
try: Reply kindly to the next reminder someone shares, even if it is not your style.

title: And what if the one stopping him denies and turns away?
subtitle: Now look at the other side
then: After asking about the one who prays, the verses turn to the one who forbids. {trap}What if he is the one who denies and turns away?{/trap} The questions set the two men side by side so the listener can judge.
now: You are in an argument and sure you are the reasonable one. {idea}Try swapping places for a second.{/idea} {trap}Is it possible you are the one turning away?{/trap}
old: In any conflict, I am usually the one in the right.
new: I should check whether I am the one denying and turning away.
try: In your next disagreement, ask yourself once: what if I am the one in the wrong?

title: Does he not know that Allah sees?
subtitle: The sentence that changes everything
then: Ibn Kathir: does he not know that {idea}Allah sees him and hears his words{/idea}, and {trap}will compensate him in full{/trap} for what he has done? The whole surah turns on this short question.
now: You are alone in the car, the office, the bedroom, phone in hand. Nobody will know. {idea}Allah sees.{/idea} {reward}He also sees the late-night prayer no one else knows about.{/reward}
old: If nobody sees it, it does not really count.
new: Allah sees everything I do, the wrong and the good alike.
try: Today, do one good deed only Allah will see, and skip one wrong only He would see.

title: If he does not stop, he will be seized.
subtitle: A warning that still leaves room to stop
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {trap}if he does not recant from his discord and obstinacy{/trap}. The warning begins with if. {reward}Even for Abu Jahl, there was a moment to stop.{/reward}
now: You know there is something you keep doing that you should not. The warning signs keep coming. {reward}The word if means you still have time.{/reward} Stopping today is still possible.
old: I have gone too far to stop now.
new: The warning starts with if; I can still stop.
try: Pick one wrong you keep repeating and decide today when you will stop.

title: A lying, sinful forelock.
subtitle: The front of the head, where pride shows
then: Ibn Kathir: the forelock of Abu Jahl was {trap}lying in its statements and sinful in its actions{/trap}. The forelock is the front of the head, the part a proud man holds high. {idea}It is named for both its words and its deeds.{/idea}
now: You carry your head high in the meeting while padding the numbers. {trap}The verse puts the lie and the pride in the same place.{/trap} {idea}Lowering your head in sujood is the opposite of that.{/idea}
old: What I say and what I do are separate things.
new: My words and my actions are both written in the same record.
try: Correct one small exaggeration or untruth you told recently.

title: Then let him call his gang.
subtitle: His boast about numbers, answered
then: Ibn Abbas reported that Abu Jahl threatened the Prophet ﷺ and said: {trap}By Allah, I have the most kinsmen of this valley with me{/trap}. Then Allah revealed: let him call his council. {idea}His crowd was his whole argument.{/idea}
now: In the group chat, everyone has sided against you, and it feels like that settles who is right. {idea}A crowd is not a proof.{/idea} And when you are the one with the crowd, it is not a licence.
old: Whoever has more people on their side wins.
new: Numbers do not decide right and wrong; Allah does.
try: Next time you feel outnumbered for doing right, hold your position calmly once.

title: We will call the angels of Hell.
subtitle: His side against Allah's side
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}the angels of torment{/idea}, so he may know whose side will win. Ibn Abbas said if he had called his people, {idea}the angels would have seized him at once{/idea}. Abu Hurayrah reported that he once drew near, then {reward}retreated, saying he saw a ditch of fire between them{/reward}.
now: You stand up for what is right at work and feel completely alone. {reward}You are not as alone as it looks.{/reward} The one who prays has protection no one else can see.
old: If I stand for the truth, I will be on my own.
new: Allah defends those who worship Him in ways I cannot see.
try: Make a short dua for protection today before you face something difficult.

title: Do not obey him. Bow down and come close.
subtitle: The answer to threats is prostration
then: Ibn Kathir: {idea}pray wherever you wish and do not worry about him, for Allah will protect you{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}the closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so make much dua{/reward}.
now: The pressure is on: people mocking, deadlines crushing, a voice telling you to drop your prayers for a while. {reward}The surah ends with: put your forehead down and come closer.{/reward} The answer to every threat is the floor of the prayer mat.
old: When life pushes on me, I need to stand stronger on my own.
new: When pressure comes, I go down in sujood and draw closer to Allah.
try: In your next sujood, stay a little longer and ask Allah for something you need.
